title: The Last Spire Revisited
premise: Rafael Eriksen, a temple scribe bound by debt to the Order that outlawed magic, has spent two decades selling harmless charms while hiding the small magic of their own blood. When a mute child arrives speaking the First Tongue—the language spoken before kingdoms, and before the court beneath the mountain stole its speakers' souls—Rafael learns the child is the last unclaimed soul from a bargain the founders made. To free the child, Rafael must descend into the Undercourt, where debts are currency and truth is the only weapon that cuts. In the end, Rafael pays their own twenty years of hidden magic as the price, shattering the founding bargain, freeing the mountain's stolen souls, and choosing exile over belonging—only to find the child, and a rebuilt city, waiting to claim them as family.
about_author: Marguerite Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing condemned manuscripts in a northern university library. They write fantasy about people whose loyalties cost more than their lives.

chapters.title: Ink and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. A day in the life: copying edicts against magic by morning, selling charms in the night market by evening, both crimes under the Order's nose. Establishes Rafael's debt-bond, their quiet self-contempt, and the city of Vell's fear-thinned streets. Emotional beat: weary complicity—Rafael has made peace with being small.

chapters.title: The Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. During a storm, a child of perhaps eight appears at Rafael's door, speaking words no living tongue should hold—and the wards on Rafael's shop answer them. The child cannot speak Common, cannot say their name, but writes one word in ash: MINE. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in tenderness; Rafael takes the child in knowing it is treason.

chapters.title: What the Ash Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael consults forbidden archives and an old heretic lexicon, learning the child speaks the First Tongue—the language of souls once sold to the court beneath Mount Cael. Every speaker was claimed; this child was missed. Emotional beat: the past is not dead; it is owed.

chapters.title: The Order Knocks
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Inquisitor Serane Halvorsen arrives investigating reports of 'unlicensed resonance.' Rafael lies badly, then well, and buys time at the cost of a favor owed. The child hides beneath the floor among Rafael's contraband. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve—lying for someone else feels different than lying for oneself.

chapters.title: A Debt Called In
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael's creditor, Master Ondrel of the Order, demands repayment or service: inform on the heretic circles of Vell. Rafael realizes the net is closing from every side. Meanwhile the child begins teaching Rafael the First Tongue in dreams. Emotional beat: suffocation; every door leads deeper into the trap.

chapters.title: The Heretic's Kitchen
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael seeks out Wrenna, a disgraced priestess running a soup kitchen that doubles as a sanctuary for the magically marked. Wrenna recognizes what the child is and names the price of help: Rafael must steal the Ledger of Debts from the Order's own vault. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; belonging offered at a terrible exchange rate.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Language
chapters.summary: POV the child (rendered through Rafael's close third). Through shared dreams, we see the child's memory: the mountain court, the singing, the moment the others were taken. The child's name surfaces—Isolde. Emotional beat: grief given language at last; Rafael stops seeing a mystery and sees a survivor.

chapters.title: The Vault Beneath the Temple
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The heist: Rafael uses scribe credentials to enter the archive, guided by Wrenna's contacts. They find the Ledger—and discover their own name in it, entered the day they were born. Their debt was never money. It was collateral. Emotional beat: betrayal; the life Rafael thought they chose was purchased.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Interest
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Reeling, Rafael deciphers the entry: their parents sold Rafael's latent magic to the Undercourt to buy the city's protection. Rafael has been a held asset all along. Isolde comforts them in the First Tongue, and Rafael understands her fully for the first time. Emotional beat: identity collapse, then the first true bond.

chapters.title: Serane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Serane. The inquisitor, investigating the vault breach, finds traces of Rafael—but hesitates. A flashback reveals Serane's sister was taken by the Order for magic years ago. She offers Rafael a deal: the child, and she looks away. Emotional beat: the antagonist revealed as a mirror; loyalty versus truth embodied.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael refuses Serane's bargain and warns Wrenna that the sanctuary will fall within days. The heretics scatter; some curse Rafael for bringing the storm. Ondrel, suspicious, moves up his deadline. Emotional beat: isolation as the cost of principle; Rafael loses every safe harbor at once.

chapters.title: The Road Down
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. With Wrenna's map and Isolde's instinct, Rafael flees Vell toward Mount Cael, pursued by Order riders. On the road, Isolde speaks her first word of Common: 'Home.' She means the mountain. Emotional beat: grim hope; the destination is also the danger.

chapters.title: Gates of Salt and Bone
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. At the mountain's sealed gate, they meet Brannoc, a gatekeeper who traded his voice to the Undercourt long ago and communicates in gesture and written verse. He warns: the court does not steal souls—it buys them, and buyers always collect. Emotional beat: awe curdling into clarity about the true enemy.

chapters.title: The Market of Owed Things
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Descending through the Undercourt's outer galleries, Rafael witnesses the soul-trade: memories pawned, names mortgaged, centuries of bargains humming in the stone. Isolde's presence makes the walls sing. They are noticed. Emotional beat: horror at scale; corruption here is not wickedness but bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Audience with the Tallyman
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The Tallyman, the court's ancient accountant-king, receives them courteously. He reveals the full contract: Isolde is the final outstanding entry of the founding bargain, and Rafael's own magic is pledged against it. He offers Rafael a choice: take Isolde home and forfeit everything, or leave her and be freed of all debt. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: POV Isolde/Rafael interwoven. In the holding cells, Isolde shows Rafael the other captive souls—not monsters, just people who kept choosing safety over each other until nothing remained. Rafael understands the Tallyman's power runs entirely on consented small betrayals. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized; loyalty is not feeling but repeated refusal.

chapters.title: The Loophole in the Blood
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Studying the founding contract, Rafael finds the flaw: the bargain required 'all speakers of the First Tongue,' but Isolde, having learned Common, is now a speaker of two—and a contract that claims a bilingual soul can be contested by either tongue. But contesting requires a counterparty willing to pledge equal value. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity; the pen is finally mightier.

chapters.title: Serane Descends
chapters.summary: POV Serane. Having tracked them, Serane enters the Undercourt seeking her sister's soul—and finds it already spent, dissolved into the Tallyman's ledgers decades ago. Grief breaks her loyalty to the Order. She finds Rafael and offers the thing she swore she never would: her testimony. Emotional beat: an enemy converted by loss into an ally.

chapters.title: The Contest of Tongues
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Before the assembled court, Rafael contests the contract, arguing in flawless First Tongue taught by Isolde herself—the debtor's own gift voiding the claim. The Tallyman counters by demanding equal value pledged. Rafael offers their twenty years of hoarded magic, every charm, every hidden spark. Emotional beat: climax of sacrifice; Rafael gives away the self they were protecting.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: POV Rafael/Serane. The contract burns. The mountain shakes as every pawned soul is released—a rising chorus in the First Tongue. The Tallyman, his books emptied, crumbles into dust and ink. Serane holds the collapsing tunnel so Rafael and Isolde can escape with the freed souls streaming toward the surface. Emotional beat: catharsis; the whole mountain exhales.

chapters.title: Exile's Welcome
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Above ground, the freed souls disperse to whatever remains of their lives. Rafael, magicless and officially a traitor, expects nothing—but Wrenna's network has spread the story, and Vell's outlawed faithful begin arriving at the old spire ruins asking Rafael to teach them what Isolde taught. Emotional beat: quiet astonishment; belonging arrives unbidden.

chapters.title: The Spire, Revisited
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, coda. One year later: the ruined spire is a school, Serane guards its door, and Isolde teaches children two languages. Rafael, still unable to work even the smallest charm, writes the grammar of the First Tongue by hand. On the last page, Isolde adds a word in ash, as she did that first night: HOME. Emotional beat: grace; the family you choose outlasts the power you lose.
